newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Bayer H1 profit up on foreign growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bayer H1 profit up on foreign growth.

text.p: German chemicals and pharmaceutical group Bayer AG on Tuesday reaffirmed its forecast for 1997 sales to top 50 billion marks ($27.3 billion), with its foreign business providing the main engine for growth.
In common with other major German exporters, Bayer reaped the benefits of the stronger dollar which made its products cheaper abroad.
"The greatest stimulus to growth came from our companies outside Europe, which recorded seven percent higher sales overall," Bayer said.
Of this, the increase in group sales was driven mainly by the continuing upward business trend in the Americas.
"In the second quarter, however, our German companies also showed a substantial improvement."
Bayer said that 1.3 billion marks of the 2.6 billion mark sales hike was attributable to favourable exchange rates.
Another 1.7 billion marks came from higher volumes and 300 million from newly acquired business, while against this, price pressure diminished the sales figures by 700 million marks.
Ronald Koehler, chemicals analyst at BHF Bank in Frankfurt, said a conference call with analysts in the afternoon had not revealed anything "surprisingly new."
"The healthcare sector took a hit in the first half, but the company said it would make up these losses in the second half," Koehler said.
"The company pointed out that it had already booked an 80-million-mark restructuring charge in the chemical sector and that it expected better second-half earnings," Koehler said.
"At the same time, earnings in Polymers were held at high levels in the first half despite price pressures, and Bayer said there would be more pressure in the second half," he said.
Koehler is not expecting major increases in earnings per share (EPS) in the current year, with forecasts at four marks per share, but for 1998 is expecting EPS of 4.70 marks.
Bayer -- the last of the so-called Big Three among German chemical companies to report its interim results -- also said it was confident that net earnings in the full-year would rise.
"For the second half of the year we are confident that lively demand will continue while foreign exchange rates will stabilise," the group said in its interim statement.
"As such we are confident that we can report sales of 50 billion marks for the full year and full-year net profit above the previous year," Bayer said. Net profit in 1996 was 2.7 billion marks.
Net profit rose 13 percent to 1.7 billion marks from 1.5 billion in the first-half of 1996, while sales rose 11 percent to 27.4 billion marks in the first six months of the year.
Group operating profit rose six percent to three billion marks, while group cash flow was up 18 percent at 3.2 billion marks in the first half.
Shares in Bayer were on a rollercoaster ride in early share trade, at one point falling nearly two percent, but the share price recovered after the figures were announced.
In late afternoon trade Bayer shares were up 1.41 marks at 71.70 marks. The overall IBIS DAX index was up 1.81 percent at 4,153.94 points.

Group pre-tax profit was 2.8 billion marks in the first half of 1997, a rise of 2.5 percent. Analysts polled by Reuters expected Bayer to post pre-tax profit of between 2.8 and 2.86 billion marks, an increase of between 2.6 and five percent.
Bayer's sales had been expected to rise to between 26.5 and 26.9 billion marks from 24.80 billion marks in the year-ago period, marking an advance of between 6.9 and 8.1 percent.
--Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.834 German Marks)
